domainDescription: Manage interplanetary shipments, space station docking bays, crew manifests, fusion fuel reserves, and mission control telemetry.

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Command, we are building the Orbital Logistics Control System from scratch. Start by creating a `vessels` table with `vessel_id` (INT), `vessel_name` (TEXT), and `class_type` (TEXT).

hints.tier1Concept: Use CREATE TABLE to define the structure of the vessels registry.
hints.tier3Solution: CREATE TABLE vessels (vessel_id INT, vessel_name TEXT, class_type TEXT);

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='vessels';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Three vessels are cleared for registry: (1,'Ares IV','Heavy Freighter'), (2,'Hermes Scout','Recon Class'), (3,'Europa Station','Orbital Platform').

hints.tier1Concept: Insert multiple rows with a single INSERT using comma-separated VALUES.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
INSERT INTO vessels VALUES
  (1,'Ares IV','Heavy Freighter'),
  (2,'Hermes Scout','Recon Class'),
  (3,'Europa Station','Orbital Platform');
hints.tier3Solution: INSERT INTO vessels VALUES (1,'Ares IV','Heavy Freighter'),(2,'Hermes Scout','Recon Class'),(3,'Europa Station','Orbital Platform');

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM vessels;

hints.tier2Scaffold: SELECT vessel_name, class_type FROM vessels WHERE vessel_id = 1;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT vessel_name, class_type FROM vessels WHERE vessel_id = 1;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT vessel_name FROM vessels WHERE vessel_id=1;

hints.tier2Scaffold: ALTER TABLE vessels ADD COLUMN status TEXT;
hints.tier3Solution: ALTER TABLE vessels ADD COLUMN status TEXT;

hints.tier2Scaffold:

UPDATE vessels SET status = 'DOCKED' WHERE vessel_id = 3;
hints.tier3Solution: UPDATE vessels SET status = 'ACTIVE' WHERE vessel_id IN (1, 2); UPDATE vessels SET status = 'DOCKED' WHERE vessel_id = 3;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Show each cargo item along with the vessel name and the number of crew on that vessel. Use JOINs and subqueries.

hints.tier1Concept: JOIN cargo to vessels on vessel_id, then JOIN a crew-count subquery.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
SELECT c.cargo_type, v.vessel_name, cc.crew_count
FROM cargo c
JOIN vessels v ON c.vessel_id = v.vessel_id
JOIN (SELECT vessel_id, COUNT(*) as crew_count FROM crew GROUP BY vessel_id) cc
  ON c.vessel_id = cc.vessel_id;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT c.cargo_type, v.vessel_name, cc.crew_count FROM cargo c JOIN vessels v ON c.vessel_id = v.vessel_id JOIN (SELECT vessel_id, COUNT(*) as crew_count FROM crew GROUP BY vessel_id) cc ON c.vessel_id = cc.vessel_id;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM cargo c JOIN vessels v ON c.vessel_id=v.vessel_id JOIN (SELECT vessel_id, COUNT(*) as n FROM crew GROUP BY vessel_id) cc ON c.vessel_id=cc.vessel_id;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Classify each fuel depot's reserve status: reserves > 400 is 'CRITICAL_SURPLUS', > 200 is 'ADEQUATE', else 'LOW'.

hints.tier1Concept: Use CASE WHEN with multiple conditions to classify numeric ranges.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
SELECT station_name, fuel_type, reserves_tons,
  CASE
    WHEN reserves_tons > 400 THEN 'CRITICAL_SURPLUS'
    WHEN reserves_tons > 200 THEN 'ADEQUATE'
    ELSE 'LOW'
  END as supply_status
FROM fuel_depots;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT station_name, fuel_type, reserves_tons, CASE WHEN reserves_tons > 400 THEN 'CRITICAL_SURPLUS' WHEN reserves_tons > 200 THEN 'ADEQUATE' ELSE 'LOW' END as supply_status FROM fuel_depots;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM fuel_depots;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Show all vessels along with any cargo they carry, including vessels with no cargo assigned (Europa Station has none). Use LEFT JOIN.

hints.tier1Concept: LEFT JOIN returns all vessels regardless of whether they have matching cargo rows.
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT v.vessel_name, c.cargo_type, c.mass_tons FROM vessels v LEFT JOIN cargo c ON v.vessel_id = c.vessel_id;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM vessels v LEFT JOIN cargo c ON v.vessel_id=c.vessel_id;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Find the vessel carrying the most total cargo mass. Use a subquery to get the max total and match it.

hints.tier1Concept: Use a subquery to compute the MAX of aggregated totals.
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT vessel_id, SUM(mass_tons) as total FROM cargo GROUP BY vessel_id HAVING total = (SELECT MAX(total_mass) FROM (SELECT SUM(mass_tons) as total_mass FROM cargo GROUP BY vessel_id));

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT vessel_id FROM cargo GROUP BY vessel_id ORDER BY SUM(mass_tons) DESC LIMIT 1;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Use a CTE to compute each vessel's total cargo mass, then join with vessels to show vessel_name and total_mass.

hints.tier1Concept: WITH cte AS (...) SELECT ... FROM cte JOIN ...
hints.tier3Solution: WITH vessel_load AS (SELECT vessel_id, SUM(mass_tons) as total_mass FROM cargo GROUP BY vessel_id) SELECT v.vessel_name, vl.total_mass FROM vessels v JOIN vessel_load vl ON v.vessel_id = vl.vessel_id;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM (WITH vl AS (SELECT vessel_id FROM cargo GROUP BY vessel_id) SELECT v.vessel_name FROM vessels v JOIN vl ON v.vessel_id=vl.vessel_id);

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Create a view `mission_manifest` that shows vessel_name, crew count, and total cargo mass for each active vessel.

hints.tier1Concept: Use CREATE VIEW with a query that JOINs vessels, crew (counted), and cargo (summed).
hints.tier2Scaffold:
CREATE VIEW mission_manifest AS
SELECT v.vessel_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.crew_id) as crew_count,
  SUM(ca.mass_tons) as cargo_mass
FROM vessels v
LEFT JOIN crew c ON v.vessel_id = c.vessel_id
LEFT JOIN cargo ca ON v.vessel_id = ca.vessel_id
WHERE v.status = 'ACTIVE'
GROUP BY v.vessel_id;
hints.tier3Solution: CREATE VIEW mission_manifest AS SELECT v.vessel_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.crew_id) as crew_count, SUM(ca.mass_tons) as cargo_mass FROM vessels v LEFT JOIN crew c ON v.vessel_id = c.vessel_id LEFT JOIN cargo ca ON v.vessel_id = ca.vessel_id WHERE v.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY v.vessel_id;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='view' AND name='mission_manifest';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Rank each crew member within their vessel by seniority (Commander=1, Pilot=2, Engineer=3, Scientist=4) using CASE + RANK().

hints.tier1Concept: Use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY vessel_id ORDER BY CASE rank ...) to assign seniority ranks.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
SELECT name, rank, vessel_id,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY vessel_id
    ORDER BY CASE rank
      WHEN 'Commander' THEN 1
      WHEN 'Pilot' THEN 2
      WHEN 'Engineer' THEN 3
      ELSE 4
    END
  ) as seniority_rank
FROM crew;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT name, rank, vessel_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY vessel_id ORDER BY CASE rank WHEN 'Commander' THEN 1 WHEN 'Pilot' THEN 2 WHEN 'Engineer' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END) as seniority_rank FROM crew;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM (SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY vessel_id ORDER BY crew_id) as rn FROM crew);

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Compute cumulative fuel reserves at Olympus Station ordered by depot_id using SUM() OVER.

hints.tier1Concept: SUM() OVER (WHERE station_name='Olympus Station' ORDER BY depot_id) gives running total.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
SELECT depot_id, fuel_type, reserves_tons,
  SUM(reserves_tons) OVER (PARTITION BY station_name ORDER BY depot_id) as cumulative_reserves
FROM fuel_depots
WHERE station_name = 'Olympus Station';
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT depot_id, fuel_type, reserves_tons, SUM(reserves_tons) OVER (PARTITION BY station_name ORDER BY depot_id) as cumulative_reserves FROM fuel_depots WHERE station_name = 'Olympus Station';

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM (SELECT SUM(reserves_tons) OVER (PARTITION BY station_name ORDER BY depot_id) as cr FROM fuel_depots WHERE station_name='Olympus Station');

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Find all crew members who are assigned to a vessel that has at least one cargo item, using EXISTS.

hints.tier3Solution: SELECT c.name, c.vessel_id FROM crew c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cargo ca WHERE ca.vessel_id = c.vessel_id);

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM crew c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cargo ca WHERE ca.vessel_id = c.vessel_id);

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Final Operations Report: use three CTEs to calculate crew_count per vessel, total_cargo per vessel, and total_fuel per station, then present a summary.

hints.tier1Concept: Chain multiple CTEs with commas in a single WITH block.
hints.tier3Solution: WITH crew_counts AS (SELECT vessel_id, COUNT(*) as crew_count FROM crew GROUP BY vessel_id), cargo_totals AS (SELECT vessel_id, SUM(mass_tons) as total_cargo FROM cargo GROUP BY vessel_id) SELECT v.vessel_name, cc.crew_count, ct.total_cargo FROM vessels v LEFT JOIN crew_counts cc ON v.vessel_id = cc.vessel_id LEFT JOIN cargo_totals ct ON v.vessel_id = ct.vessel_id;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM vessels v LEFT JOIN (SELECT vessel_id, COUNT(*) as n FROM crew GROUP BY vessel_id) cc ON v.vessel_id=cc.vessel_id;
